title: What Is HARP? Nova Scotia's Home Heating Assistance Rebate Explained
desc: HARP is Nova Scotia's $400 heating rebate for lower-income households. See who qualifies, what heat counts, how to apply by March 31, 2027, and how to check status.
h1: What Is HARP? Nova Scotia's Home Heating Assistance Rebate Explained
crumb: What Is HARP? Nova Scotia Heating Rebate
lead: HARP stands for the Heating Assistance Rebate Program. It gives lower-income Nova Scotia households $400 toward the cost of heating their home.
callout: Short answer: HARP pays $400 per household. You must pay your own home heat. If you live alone, your 2025 net income must be $30,000 or less. If you live with others, your combined 2025 net household income must be $45,000 or less. Apply by March 31, 2027.
sections: $400 for each household, according to the Province of Nova Scotia. It is a one-time payment for the 2026-27 application period. You can apply from October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
Who qualifies for the Nova Scotia heating rebate?

You must pay for your own home heat. Then you need to meet one of these:

  • You live alone with no kids or dependents, and your 2025 net income was $30,000 or less.
  • You live with kids, dependents or other adults, and your combined 2025 net household income was $45,000 or less.
  • You get Income Assistance.
  • You get the Guaranteed Income Supplement or the Allowance from Service Canada.

Net income is the amount on line 23600 of your 2025 tax return.

Almost any fuel counts if you pay for it yourself, such as oil, electricity, natural gas, wood or pellets. These do not count:

  • Heat that is included in your rent.
  • Heat for a rental property you own, or other income or investment property.
  • Heat for a cottage or other seasonal or recreation property.
  • Heat for a business.
  • Electric heat if your home uses less than 5,000 kilowatt hours of electricity a year.

Renters who pay their own electric heat can apply. The province has a Landlord Declaration Form for that. There are also forms for people who cut their own firewood or bought wood without a receipt.

1. Find the 2025 net income for every adult in your home.
  2. Get each adult's Social Insurance Number and date of birth.
  3. Have your 2025 Notice of Assessment and a recent heating bill or receipt ready.
  4. Apply online (you need an email address) or print the paper form and mail it. Paper forms must be postmarked by March 31, 2027.
  5. Save your confirmation number.

It costs nothing to apply. The province's apply page has the form and the full list of papers.
How to check your HARP status

If you applied online, use the province's status page with your confirmation number and postal code. We walk through it, with payment timing, in our guide to payment dates and how to check your status.

HARP is $400. It helps with one winter and does not change your home. If you want a lower bill every winter, look at a Home Energy Assessment through Efficiency Nova Scotia (up to $5,000 in rebates for any homeowner) or HomeWarming (free upgrades for lower-income homeowners). The old heat pump programs have closed. Our heat pump update explains what is left.
